relations.note: PhD and ForMathlib copies of the same API. Differences are checked per module; downstream adoption is tracked separately.
The organised copy omits some interfaces and has different imports. Its location alone does not establish that it can replace the original.
The general coefficient-ring interface in HasCoeffsIn compared with the specialised integer/complex interface in PhD.
An organised copy of the j-function and expansions. Some declarations have been split or have not been migrated.
The general HNF implementation exists both within PhD and in the top-level ForMathlib tree.
The rank-two and general matrix approaches have different scopes. A complete interface migration proof has not been registered in the dashboard.
The manifold predicates and growth API have entered the current implementation. The bundled-class interface remains experimental.
Comparison.lean establishes equivalence of local fractions and chart predicates on one-dimensional analytic complex manifolds. The equivalence is restricted to those hypotheses.
Bridge modules compare the analytic quotient with sheaf sections and record a RingEquiv within the stated scope.
An alternative proof of 11.1(i) only. Its exclusive deferred tickets are kept separate from results still shared by other work.
The two sides establish results about the plane model/function field and the actual modular curve respectively. The final comparison must connect them.

migrations.title: q-expansion Basic: confirm the shared copy and switch consumers
migrations.notes: A corresponding copy already exists. Check dependencies and the API, then select the downstream scope. This is a manually recorded preparation stage, not a claim that the current target or its consumers have been verified.

migrations.title: Laurent q-expansion: reconcile differences and shared interfaces
migrations.notes: Some interfaces are omitted from one Basic version. Check which results are still used downstream. Candidate consumers are recorded in configuration; the snapshot helps inspect actual imports.

migrations.title: General HNF: adopt the top-level ForMathlib entry point
migrations.notes: This item covers only the organised copies of the general matrix version; the rank-two approach remains. Check each entry point for compatibility: the two definitions with the same names cannot simply be imported together.
